name: Systems Mapping
description:
Systems mapping visualises components of a complex situation and the relationships between them. Depending on the purpose, maps may include actors, resources, institutions, causal relationships, flows and feedback loops.

The method helps designers move beyond isolated problems and consider how outcomes emerge from interconnected conditions.
whenToUse: Use systems mapping when a challenge involves multiple actors and interacting causes and when intervening in one part of the situation may create consequences elsewhere.
steps: Define a provisional boundary for the system.
Identify significant actors, elements and resources.
Place them on a shared mapping surface.
Draw relationships and flows between elements.
Identify reinforcing and balancing relationships where relevant.
Look for clusters, dependencies and feedback.
Identify missing perspectives and challenge the system boundary.
Use the map to locate questions, leverage points and potential consequences of intervention.
Revise the map as understanding develops.
lookOutFor: A system map is a model constructed for a purpose, not a complete representation of reality.
Avoid equating visual complexity with analytical depth.

resources.citation: Meadows, D. H. (2008). *Thinking in Systems*. Chelsea Green.
Jones, P. & Van Ael, K. (2022). *Design Journeys through Complex Systems*. BIS Publishers.
